headline: Attleboro couple died in home fire where investigators found no working alarms
dek: State fire officials say the cause of the blaze and the couple's deaths remains under investigation, while the scene has renewed attention to smoke and carbon-monoxide alarms in older residents' homes.
body: An Attleboro couple was found dead in a home where investigators found no working smoke or carbon-monoxide alarms, Massachusetts fire officials said Thursday. The finding came after a welfare check at 32 Andover Avenue, where responders discovered evidence of a significant earlier fire.

The Bristol County District Attorney's Office identified the residents as Carol Courtemanche, 78, and Paul Courtemanche, 76. The [Massachusetts Department of Fire Services](https://www.mass.gov/news/no-working-smoke-alarms-in-tragic-attleboro-fire) said the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner will determine the cause and manner of their deaths. That determination has not been announced, and officials have not said when the fire began or how long the couple may have been exposed to it.

The response began on Oct. 14 after a home health aide requested a health-and-welfare check, according to the [Attleboro Fire Department](https://attleborofire.com/2026/10/14/attleboro-police-fire-investigating-two-deaths-at-andover-avenue-home/). Police and firefighters were unable to make contact and forced entry. Inside, they found the two adults and a cat dead, with fire damage and heavy soot in the single-family home. The department's preliminary account described the incident as non-suspicious, but left both the deaths and the fire under investigation.

State Police fire investigators assigned to the State Fire Marshal's Office worked with the Attleboro police and fire departments, State Police detectives assigned to the Bristol County district attorney and the Department of Fire Services' Code Compliance and Enforcement Unit. Investigators said they considered witness interviews, the scene and other evidence and were looking at accidental factors. They said they do not believe the fire was intentionally set.

The absence of working alarms is a confirmed condition at this scene, not a finding that by itself establishes how the couple died. The state has not released an ignition source, a timeline, or a final medical conclusion. Those distinctions matter in a case where the physical evidence was discovered after the fire was no longer an active emergency. [NBC Boston](https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/attleborough-death-investigation/4030997/) reported that the fire department extinguished a smoldering fire on the first floor after the welfare check.

The state fire marshal's office used the case to repeat a basic warning with particular importance for older residents and anyone living alone: smoke alarms should be installed on every level and near sleeping areas, and carbon-monoxide alarms are needed where that hazard can exist. Officials said more than half of Massachusetts fire deaths this year have involved residents age 65 or older. The release did not provide a statewide death total in the same statement, so that comparison should not be read as a count of the Attleboro case or as a final annual statistic.

Attleboro residents are left with a local tragedy and an unanswered set of questions. The investigation will have to establish the fire's origin and cause and connect those findings, if possible, to the medical examiner's conclusions. Until those steps are complete, authorities have provided no public basis for deciding whether the fire began accidentally, whether smoke conditions were involved in the deaths, or whether any other factor contributed.

For families checking on older relatives, the immediate lesson is practical rather than speculative: test alarms, replace missing or failed units, and make sure someone can hear alerts from sleeping areas. In Attleboro, however, officials have not announced a broader neighborhood hazard, evacuation order or criminal allegation. The next public information is expected to come from the ongoing investigation and the medical examiner's findings.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Attleboro fire deaths linked to home without working alarms
seoDescription: Massachusetts fire officials say an Attleboro couple died after a home fire where investigators found no working smoke or carbon-monoxide alarms.
